correctness.rationale: Exact graph neighbourhoods produce the two parity-specific update laws. A symmetric odd-field Lyapunov identity proves eventual period at most two for every n. For even n the image is \(S\times S\) with a coordinate involution; for odd n a complete classification by the two central cardinality layers and four extreme corners yields the fixed and unique two-cycle counts. Labelled combinatorial counting and Stirling asymptotics are exact. All \(2^{2n}\) states at \(3\le n\le9\) were checked directly by packaged code; the proof is not inferred from finite tests.

value.rationale: A complete, labelled fixed-and-period-two census across a standard regular dense bipartite graph family directly addresses the known difficulty of Boolean majority attractor enumeration. The striking parity bifurcation is structural: even n has a one-step-to-periodic image of density asymptotic \(2/(\pi n)\), while odd n has only one nontrivial two-cycle and already-recurrent density asymptotic \(\sqrt{2n/\pi}2^{-n}\). The effect is not a change of variable or textbook period-two corollary, and it provides a concrete comparative benchmark for how adding one matched vertex pair changes majority recurrence.
